what: All Weather is a mix of stocks, bonds, gold and commodities built so that no single economic season can wreck it. Each asset does well in a different season (growth up or down, inflation up or down), so the risk is spread evenly across all four.
caveat: This is a teaching model built from Dalio's public principles, not Bridgewater's actual positions, and not advice.

sleeves.why: Growth is still holding up, so keep most of the stock sleeve. Trim a little because rising rates squeeze stock valuations, and late cycle tightening raises slowdown odds.
sleeves.dashboard_fit: Names that win when inflation runs hot: energy producers outside the Gulf, defense contractors with multiyear budgets, and AI infrastructure with real earnings that sits in the buy zone. Avoid long duration growth with no profits.

sleeves.why: Long bonds lose the most when inflation and rates rise, so this is the biggest cut. Keep some, because they protect you if growth suddenly breaks.
sleeves.dashboard_fit: None directly. This sleeve is the crash cushion, not a stock idea.

sleeves.why: Keep as is. Shorter bonds fall far less than long bonds when rates rise, and they now pay a solid yield.
sleeves.dashboard_fit: None directly. Think of it as dry powder that still earns interest.

sleeves.why: New sleeve for this season. TIPS pay more when inflation rises, so they replace part of the long bond sleeve.
sleeves.dashboard_fit: None directly. It is the bond sleeve that likes inflation.

sleeves.why: Gold tends to hold value when inflation, debt and geopolitical risk are all high, and all three are high now.
sleeves.dashboard_fit: Gold and silver miners and royalty companies on the critical materials theme, only when the chart and buy zone agree.

sleeves.why: Commodities are the classic rising inflation winner. With Brent above $100 and Hormuz mostly shut, energy is leading.
sleeves.dashboard_fit: Oil and gas producers outside the Gulf, copper and uranium miners, and fertilizer makers on the critical materials and AI power themes.

tilt_why: In the rising inflation season, long bonds and expensive growth stocks usually lose and real assets usually win. So this tilt moves 20 points out of long Treasuries and 5 out of stocks, and puts them into inflation linked bonds, gold and commodities. Growth is still positive, so stocks stay a large sleeve, and some long bonds stay in case the late cycle tightening breaks growth.
history: In 2022, when inflation surged and the Fed hiked fast, stocks and bonds fell together: long Treasuries (TLT) fell about 30% and intermediate Treasuries (IEF) about 10%, and the RPAR risk parity ETF lost more than 30% versus about 18% for the S&P 500 (VOO), so a bond heavy All Weather mix gave no shelter that year.
